THE FEDERAL LAND TRACT SALES — A PURCHASE, AND NEVER A RESIDENCE. The Illinois State Archives' Public Domain Land Tract Sales register enters this person 4 times, as “PEARSON HIRAM”, 1836-06-28: 4 lots in the platted town — lot 10 of block 1 in the town the register codes CHIV (L10BL1CHIV, as printed); lot 7 of block 1 in the town the register codes CHI (L7BL1CHI, as printed); lot 8 of block 1 in the town the register codes CHIV (L8BL1CHIV, as printed); lot 9 of block 1 in the town the register codes CHIV (L9BL1CHIV, as printed), 0.00 acres stated in all, for $22410.00 (ls1402, ls1403, ls1404, ls1405). THE REGISTER'S OWN RESIDENCE COLUMN READS UNKNOWN on these rows: a county, a state or nothing, and never a town, which is why a purchase here places nobody. THE TOWN LOTS ARE THE PLAT ITSELF, AND THEY ARE NOT ACRES: Cook County's register describes them by lot and block in a platted town and gives them no section, no township and no acreage at all, so they add nothing to the acre figure above and $22410.00 to the money. This project does not expand the register's town codes, so which addition a lot stands in is carried as the code and not as a name. It is still a purchase and it still places nobody. A purchase and nothing more. It dates and places a transaction; it proposes no residence, and under the ratified ladder it corroborates rather than mints. Identity by the crosswalk's own rule: PEARSON HIRAM matches Hiram Pearson: the forename names Hiram Pearson of the 1 person of this surname, and the forename agrees in full. (data/research/land_sales/resident_crosswalk.json). This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. Under the ratified ladder (T-0513) a second independent source is what lifts a projected resident, and a land entry is a second source about a TRANSACTION rather than about who was living at Chicago on 1 July 1835 — a man may buy a quarter-section he never sees. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.
